echo: Our list is growing too slowly, or doesn’t exist yet, so most of our visitors leave without ever giving us a way to reach them again.
p1_h1: Most businesses are fishing in the same crowded [[10% pool]].
p1_body: Say you’re selling medicine for ulcers. Most marketing leads with the problem, which only speaks to the people who already know they have it.
sol_note: Anyone who doesn’t believe they have ulcers decides this isn’t for them, even if they’ve had stomach pain for months.
sym_note: The same person who scrolled past ulcers stops here, because this one is about something they already feel.
lead_sol: Only the 10 who already know they have ulcers pay attention. The 60 with stomach pain self-select out, sure it isn’t for them, even though it is.
lead_sym1: First, the 30 who have stomach pain but haven’t been thinking about what’s causing it start paying attention…
lead_sym: …then the 30 who never believed they had ulcers join in too. Same audience, same spend, and you’re now speaking to 70 of every 100 instead of 10.
flip_to_sym: Now tap to see what the symptom-led message reaches
flip_to_sol: Tap to compare with the problem-led message again
slice_ready: They know they have ulcers and buy immediately. Already convinced, already comparing, already halfway to a decision.
slice_open: They know they have ulcers and are open to buying when the right offer shows up. Together with the 3%, this is the pool everyone fishes in.
slice_notthink: They have stomach pain, but they aren’t thinking about what’s causing it, so they don’t feel any urgency to solve it right now.
slice_dontthink: They have stomach pain but don’t know ulcers are causing it, so the moment they see “medicine for ulcers” they self-select out, convinced it isn’t for them.
slice_not: They know for sure they don’t have ulcers. Some are completely unaware, and some are very aware but simply don’t want to work with you.
credit: By Chet Holmes, The Ultimate Sales Machine
next1: So how does this grow an email list?
p2_h1: Your list grows slowly because your sign-up only speaks to **the 10% who are ready to buy**.
p2_body: Many of your potential buyers are already circling, having seen your ads or content a few times, but they’re still unclear on what you do, why it’s different and why it matters right now, so a sign-up built for ready buyers gives them no reason to join.
tabs_lbl: Pick the business closest to yours
services_h: Mary, an executive coach, was getting 60,000+ LinkedIn views a month, but every $5,000 sale still depended on long back-and-forth DMs, so the moment she stepped back, revenue stepped back with her.
services_mcap: 1,900 joined in her first 10 days (×3 for a month), with 73–79% of quiz-takers joining her list.
services_rxs: more people joining her list every month
services_r0s: revenue, $14K → $51K a month, same organic traffic
courses_h: Samar Owais, a respected name in SaaS and e-commerce email, launched her Champion’s Challenge™ Conversion Quiz™ to give readers a reason to join that was about them, not her course.
courses_r0s: list growth, which fuelled her email course sales
products_h: A B2B2C audio company was sending 140,000 influencer visits a month to free 3D audio software for gamers, but the site never answered the question every gamer was quietly asking: “If this is similar to Dolby or Sony, why would I switch?”
products_b1: every gamer who didn’t download straight away was gone
products_a1: matched gamers to their games, then demoed the difference live
cta: Show me where my next subscribers will come from
up_next: Next question: Where does most of your traffic or audience come from today?
